newsitem.title: FRANCE: Libya accused of torturing jailed Algerian rebels.
newsitem.headline: Libya accused of torturing jailed Algerian rebels.

text.p: The Algerian Brotherhood in France, a group founded by members of the banned Islamic Salvation Front (FIS), said on Wednesday that some 500 Algerian FIS activists were being held in Libyan jails and some were being tortured.
The group said Algerian FIS activists in exile in Libya had written to it, alleging that more than 500 of their number remained in Libyan prisons nine months after a wave of arrests last summer.

None have been charged, and they were apparently jailed only because they were members of the FIS, which seeks to overthrow the Algerian government and transform the country into an Islamic republic, the group alleged.

Some of those in custody had been tortured while others had been held in isolation, blindfolded or tied to a chair for long periods, or deprived of toilet facilities for as long as 34 hours, the group said in a printed statement.
Some of those who had been detained had recently been deported to Algeria where they had since disappeared, the group said.
It urged Moslem and human rights organisations to put pressure on the Libyan authorities to investigate the matter and help put an end to alleged human rights violations.
The FIS was banned in Algeria after the authorities cancelled a 1992 general election in which the FIS had taken a commanding lead.
Groups of FIS activists have subsequently sprung up in countries around the world. An estimated 60,000 people have been killed in fighting in Algeria between government forces and Moslem guerrillas.
